title: BST Ordered Search
summary: Use the binary-search-tree ordering invariant to choose only one child subtree after comparing the target or query boundary with the current node.
recognition_signals: the tree is explicitly a BST
every left-subtree key is smaller and every right-subtree key is larger
a comparison can discard one whole child subtree
core_rules: Use BST ordering only when the invariant is guaranteed.
Runtime is O(height), so an unbalanced plain BST can degrade to linear time.
structural_steps: compare the query with the current key
return when the current node satisfies the query
move left for a smaller target or right for a larger target
continue until found or the path ends

common_confusions.distinction: Both discard an ordered region after comparison. Binary search indexes an ordered sequence; BST search follows child links in an ordered tree and costs O(tree height).
